headline: Brunson, Towns and the bench help the Knicks beat the Bucks 117-85 for their fourth straight victory
text: NEW YORK -- — Jalen Brunson scored 23 points, Karl-Anthony Towns had 21 points and 16 rebounds, and the New York Knicks beat the Milwaukee Bucks 117-85 on Tuesday night for their fourth straight victory. OG Anunoby made five 3-pointers and finished with 19 points for the Knicks, who have won six of seven since an 0-3 start. They outscored the Bucks 32-13 in the second quarter to blow open the game and then put it away in the fourth after Milwaukee had gotten back into it. The Knicks got big efforts from their bench, with no starter playing more than 28 minutes on the front end of back-to-back games. Tyler Kolek scored 12 points and provided a spark in the second quarter as the backup to Brunson, Andre Drummond grabbed 14 rebounds in 15 minutes, and Deuce McBride had eight points and New York outscored Milwaukee by 39 while he was on the floor. Jaime Jaquez Jr . scored 16 points and Ryan Rollins had 14 for the Bucks, who lost their seventh straight and fell to 1-10. They played without leading scorer Tyler Herro , who missed his first game of the season because of a bruised right knee. The Knicks led by three early in the second quarter before Anunoby and Kolek combined for the next 10 points to make it 36-23. Ousmane Dieng made a 3-pointer before Kolek scored again to ignite another 10-0 run, and Brunson and Anunoby ended the half with consecutive 3-pointers to make it 58-34. Milwaukee pulled to 85-72 after three quarters and got the first basket of the fourth, but Towns led the way as New York quickly pushed the lead beyond 20, with consecutive 3-pointers by Anunoby making it 106-78. Josh Hart missed his third straight game, this time because of an illness. He sat out the previous two because of right ankle soreness, but coach Mike Brown said he believed the starting forward was healed enough that he could have played if not for feeling sick. Up next Bucks: Host the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday. Knicks: Host Cleveland on Wednesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Jordan Goodwin scores 18 on 6 3-pointers, Suns ease past the Clippers 133-110
text: PHOENIX -- — Jordan Goodwin scored 18 points in his return from a calf injury, Devin Booker added 17 and the Phoenix Suns cruised past the Los Angeles Clippers 133-110 on Tuesday night. Phoenix shot 22 of 43 (51%) from 3-point range and had seven players score in double digits, including five who came off the bench. Luke Kennard had 14 points, Jalen Green scored 13 and Collin Gillespie added 12 points and eight assists while Khaman Maluach contributed 11 points and seven rebounds. The Suns had a 17-point halftime lead and pushed the advantage to 91-59 with four minutes left in the third quarter. They have a 3-2 record so far on their season-long, seven-game homestand. Goodwin — who signed a $19 million, three-year deal to return to the Suns during the offseason — made 6 of 7 shots from beyond the arc in just 14 minutes. He missed the past three games. The Clippers were coming off their first win in more than two weeks, but have now lost eight of their last nine games. Rui Hachimura , Baba Miller and Darius Garland all scored 13 points while Max Strus had 12. Gillespie hit a 3-pointer from 39 feet just before the halftime buzzer to give the Suns a 64-47 lead. Phoenix made 11 of 22 (50%) shots from beyond the arc before the break. Up next Clippers: Host Oklahoma City on Friday night. Suns: Host Charlotte on Thursday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Despite hurt wrist, Antetokounmpo scores 30 and Heat outlast Jazz 115-109
text: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 30 points, Davion Mitchell added 19 points, and the Miami Heat outlasted the depleted Utah Jazz 115-109 on Tuesday night. The Heat also got 14 from Pelle Larsson but needed late blocks from Klay Thompson and Bam Adebayo to secure their third win in their last four games. Antetokounmpo iced his sprained right wrist in a heavy wrap when he was on the bench but it didn’t seem to bother him on the court. He shot 12 for 21 and grabbed 11 rebounds. He now has 21,836 points and passed Gary Payton to become the 39th leading scorer in NBA history. Despite the Jazz's ninth straight loss, Utah's two teenagers gave the Jazz hope for the future. Rookie Darryn Peterson nearly set his career high (26) for the second game in a row with 25 points and Ace Bailey scored 23. Utah's Isaiah Collier , a notoriously poor shooter who had not made a 3-pointer this season, made four consecutive shots from behind the arc in the fourth quarter to cut Miami's lead to 101-93. Then Svi Mykhailiuk made back-to-back baskets to cut the lead to 112-107 in the final minute but it was too late for the Jazz, who were missing four starters to injury — Lauri Markkanen (wrist), Keyonte George (ankle), Jaren Jackson Jr . (knee), and Jusuf Nurkic (foot). Antetokounmpo's shooting sparked the Heat to a 15-2 run in the third quarter to give the Heat the cushion they needed and send them home with a 3-2 record on their five-game road trip. Larsson hit a 3-pointer with 6:58 left in the second quarter to cap a 13-1 run and make it 49-32 for Miami. The Jazz, who have been hurt by turnovers all season, had 18 to just eight for the Heat. Up next Heat: Host Cleveland on Friday night to commence a five-game homestand. Jazz: Host Orlando on Wednesday to complete the back-to-back set. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Franz Wagner scores season-high 33 points as Magic beat Kings 107-100 to snap 4-game skid
text: SACRAMENTO, Calif. -- — Franz Wagner had a season-high 33 points with seven rebounds and seven assists, Anthony Black scored 26 and the Orlando Magic beat the Sacramento Kings 107-100 on Tuesday night to snap a four-game losing streak. Wagner, who had 30 points and 11 assists in a 126-119 loss to Golden State on Saturday, made 10 of 21 from the field and 10 of 10 from the free-throw line. Black had seven rebounds, five assists and four steals. Sacramento has lost four straight overall and is 0-6 at home this season. Zach LaVine led the Kings with 31 points on 10-of-16 shooting, 6 of 9 from 3-point range. Darius Acuff Jr . hit four 3-pointers and finished with 29 points. The 19-year-old Acuff has 288 points, the most by any rookie through the first 11 games of a season since Michael Jordan scored 289 for the Chicago Bulls in 1984. Wagner hit a 3 to cap an 18-5 run that made it 52-43 with 3:10 remaining in the second quarter and the Magic led the rest of the way. Domantas Sabonis , who missed Sacramento's 114-108 home loss to Miami on Sunday due to left knee soreness, was scoreless on 0-for-2 shooting in 24 minutes. The three-time All-Star and NBA rebounding champion finished with five assists and two boards. Paolo Banchero , Jalen Suggs , Jonathan Isaac and Tristan da Silva did not play for the Magic. Banchero, the 2023 NBA Rookie of the Year and an All-Star in 2024, missed his eighth consecutive game. The 6-foot-10, 23-year-old forward sustained a high ankle sprain in a 115-93 home loss to Minnesota on Oct. 23. Desmond Bane scored 15 points and Wendell Carter Jr . had 11 rebounds to go with eight points for the Magic. Up next Magic: Play Wednesday at Utah. Kings: Host Portland on Friday. ------ This story has been corrected to fix a typo in the final score. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headline: Damian Lillard scores 25 points as the Trail Blazers beat the Thunder 123-103
text: PORTLAND, Ore. -- — Damian Lillard scored 25 points and the Portland Trail Blazers snapped a two-game skid with a 123-103 victory over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday night. Deni Avdija added 24 points, eight assists and six rebounds for the Blazers in the first of back-to-back home games against Oklahoma City. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 26 points on 8-of-22 shooting for the Thunder, who had won four straight. Gilgeous-Alexander also grabbed eight rebounds but missed all four of his 3-point attempts and did not play in the fourth quarter. The Thunder are without several key players because of injuries, including Jalen Williams (ankle), Chet Holmgren (knee) and Cason Wallace (shoulder). Jaylin Williams missed his fourth game with back spasms. Oklahoma City, coming off a 114-75 victory over Washington on Saturday, acquired guard/forward Nique Clifford from Sacramento on Sunday. Clifford came off the bench and made his Thunder debut to start the second quarter. He scored on a reverse layup early in the fourth. Gilgeous-Alexander scored 12 early points and the Thunder had a 27-26 edge in the first quarter. The back-and-forth first half ended even at 59 with neither team able to build a double-digit lead. Jared McCain made a 3-pointer that put the Thunder in front 69-67, but Lillard answered with his own 3. Lillard hit back-to-back 3s to stretch Portland's lead to 79-71. Lillard made a 3 from the logo that gave Portland a 97-80 lead going into the fourth. Jrue Holiday 's 3-pointer put the Blazers up 106-89. Sidy Cissoko started for the Blazers in place of Scoot Henderson , who scored 11 points off the bench on 3-for-12 shooting. Cissoko finished with 17 points. Holiday also had 11 points off the bench, and Donovan Clingan pulled down 13 rebounds. McCain finished with 21 points for the Thunder. Up next The teams play again Wednesday in Portland. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
